nodes.title: At least two reflex corners are excluded
Large-N low-threshold stationary polygons are convex

proofs.proof_text: By @def-stationary-polygon, the derivative of \(J=A\lambda\) vanishes for every vertex displacement. Hadamard’s formula is \[ DJ[V]=A\int_{\partial P}(c-q)V\cdot\nu\,ds. \] Moving one endpoint of an effective edge while keeping the other fixed produces an affine normal velocity on that edge, and the two endpoint velocities give the independent functions \(1\) and \(s/\ell_E\). Since adjacent effective edge normals are linearly independent at a genuine corner, stationarity forces both coefficients of these two affine test functions to vanish. Rescaling \(s/\ell_E\) gives the displayed moments.

Define the divergence-free stress tensor \[ T=

The planar Airy-potential theorem for a symmetric divergence-free stress on the simply connected polygon supplies one global \(\psi\), unique up to an affine function. The two moments imply that \(

abla\Phi\}=(\Delta\Phi)^2-|D^2\Phi|^2 \] to \(P\) with corner disks removed and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). The edge terms vanish by the preceding boundary conditions, hence \(\int_P\det D^2\Phi=0\). The eigenvalues of \(D^2\Phi\) are \((\lambda u^2-c\pm|
abla u|^2)/2\), so expanding their product and using \(\int_Pu^2=1\) gives the stated identity.

The domain-independent Dirichlet heat-kernel estimate gives \(\|u\|_\infty^2\le e^2\lambda/(8\pi)\) for the normalized first eigenfunction. Under the edge-moment hypotheses, @lem-airy-identity applies, and \(\int_Pu^4\le\|u\|_\infty^2\int_Pu^2=\|u\|_\infty^2\); combining these facts yields \[ \int_P|\nabla u|^4\le \frac{e^2\lambda^3}{8\pi}. \] The same \(L^\infty\) bound gives \(\int_P|u|^4\le\|u\|_\infty^2\), so the \(W^{1,4}(P)\) norm is bounded by a constant depending only on \(A_0\) and \(\Lambda\). Since \(u\in H^1_0(P)\), its zero extension has no boundary distribution term in its weak gradient; the extension therefore lies in \(W^{1,4}(\mathbb R^2)\) with the same gradient bound. Morrey’s inequality in dimension two then gives a \(C^{0,1/2}\) representative with the same parameter dependence.

Use the similarity invariance in @def-j-functional to normalize \(A(P)=\pi\) and translate so that the Fraenkel-optimal comparison disk is \(D=B_1(0)\). The regular-polygon asymptotic is \[ \frac{J(R_M)}{\pi j^2}=1+\frac{4\zeta(3)}{M^3}+O(M^{-5}). \] The upper bound and the displayed asymptotic give \(\lambda_1(P)\le j^2(1+CN^{-3})\), while Faber–Krahn gives \(\lambda_1(P)\ge j^2\). Quantitative Faber–Krahn therefore gives \(|P\triangle D|\to0\). Let \(u_N\) be the normalized positive eigenfunction and extend it by zero. By @lem-uniform-w14, the extensions are uniformly bounded in \(W^{1,4}(\mathbb R^2)\) and hence equicontinuous and uniformly bounded. Arzelà–Ascoli gives a locally uniform limit along a subsequence. On every compact set outside \(\overline D\), the limit must vanish: otherwise the uniform Hölder bound would force a fixed positive amount of area in \(P_N\setminus D\), contradicting \(|P_N\triangle D|\to0\). The same argument gives zero trace on \(\partial D\). Since \(\|u_N\|_\infty\) is uniformly bounded, the mass outside \(D\) tends to zero; hence the limit has \(L^2(D)\) norm one. Weak lower semicontinuity gives \(\int_D|\nabla u|^2\le\liminf\lambda_1(P_N)=j^2\), while the disk Rayleigh inequality gives the reverse inequality. Thus the limit is the normalized positive disk eigenfunction \(u_0\). Uniqueness of the limit upgrades the whole sequence to local uniform convergence, and the boundary Hölder bound upgrades it to uniform convergence on \(\overline D\). Since \(u_0>0\) on \(B_{1-\eta}\), eventually \(u_N>0\) there; because the zero extension vanishes off \(P_N\), \(B_{1-\eta}\subset P_N\).The maximal conformal radius is at least \(1-\eta\) by monotonicity under inclusion and at most \(1\) by the conformal area inequality \(A(P)\ge\pi r_P^2\). In the normalization of @def-conformal-data, \(1+S=r_P^{-2}\to1\).For the quantitative rate, write the pulled-back eigenproblem as \[ -\Delta v=\lambda|1+g|^2v,\qquad v|_{\partial\mathbb D}=0, \] with the weighted \(L^2\) normalization. Put \(d(z)=1-|z|\). For \(g\in A^2\) with no constant or linear term, the Bergman pointwise estimate gives \(|g(z)|\le C\|g\|_{A^2}/d(z)\). Consequently, Hardy’s inequality and the Sobolev embedding \(H^1_0(\mathbb D)\hookrightarrow L^4(\mathbb D)\) give, for \(h,k\in H^1_0(\mathbb D)\), \[ \left|\int_{\mathbb D}2\operatorname{Re}(g)hk\right|\le C\sqrt S\,\|h\|_{H^1_0}\|k\|_{H^1_0}, \qquad \left|\int_{\mathbb D}|g|^2hk\right|\le CS\,\|h\|_{H^1_0}\|k\|_{H^1_0}. \] The second estimate uses \(|g|^2\le CS/d^2\) and \(\int |h|^2/d^2\le4\int|\nabla h|^2\). Thus the weighted Rayleigh forms are a uniformly form-analytic perturbation of the disk form, with perturbation size \(O(\sqrt S)\).Write \(g=t h\) with \(t=\sqrt S\) and \(\|h\|_{A^2}=1\). The simple disk eigenvalue is isolated by a fixed spectral gap. The form version of analytic simple-eigenvalue perturbation therefore gives, uniformly in such \(h\), \[ v=v_0+t v_1+t^2v_2+O_{H^1_0}(t^3), \qquad \lambda= j^2+t\lambda_1+t^2\lambda_2+O(t^3). \] The first variation is \(\lambda_1=-j^2\int_{\mathbb D}(h+\bar h)v_0^2=0\) because \(v_0\) is radial and \(h\) has no constant coefficient. The first-order equation for \(v_1\) is solved in angular Fourier modes; the disk spectral gap fixes its orthogonal component. For the real mode \(h=a z^n\), separation of variables and the Bessel recurrence give \[ \frac{\lambda_2}{j^2a^2}=-\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}, \qquad \rho_n=j\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{J_n(j)},\qquad 0<\rho_n<2. \] Indeed the only radial integral required is \[ \int_0^1r^{n+1}v_0(r)J_n(jr)\,dr =\frac{J_{n+1}(j)}{2\sqrt\pi(n+1)}, \] which follows by one integration by parts from the Bessel equation. Orthogonality of distinct angular modes and density of analytic polynomials extend the formula to every \(h\in A^2\). Since \(A(P)=\pi(1+S)\) in @def-conformal-data, this yields the uniform expansion \[ \frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}). \] The perturbed branch remains the first eigenvalue because its eigenfunction is the positive continuation of the disk ground state and the form perturbation is smaller than the fixed spectral gap. Since \(0<\rho_n<2\), the quadratic term is at least \(S/3\); after shrinking the universal small neighborhood, \(J(P)/(\pi j^2)-1\ge S/6\). The regular-polygon upper bound is \(O(N^{-3})\), hence \(S\le CN^{-3}\).

Under the edge-moment hypotheses @lem-edge-moments, pull @lem-airy-identity back by \(F\) and use \(F'^{-1}=1+k\) to obtain \[ \int_{\mathbb D}|
abla v|^4|1+k|^2 =\lambda^2\int_{\mathbb D}v^4|1+g|^2- rac{\lambda^2}{\pi(1+S)}. \] The perturbation expansion in @lem-near-circle-conformal gives \(|
abla v|^4=a+b_1+O(S)\), where \(a=|
abla v_0|^4\) is radial and \(b_1\) has zero circular mean. Since the constant Fourier mode of \(k\) is zero, orthogonality leaves a term \(\int a|k|^2\) on the left. On a fixed outer annulus \(a\) is bounded below, while \(k=-g/(1+g)=O(\sqrt S)\) on the inner disk. Cauchy–Schwarz and the perturbation bounds therefore give \[ T\le C\{S+\sqrt S\sqrt T+\sqrt S\,T+ST\}. \] Young’s inequality absorbs the mixed term and, for sufficiently small \(S\), the last two terms, proving \(T\le CS\).

The first-order perturbation and the second-order disk calculation from @lem-near-circle-conformal give \[ \frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}=1+S-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\rho_n}{(n+1)^2}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}), \] with \(\beta_n=n+1-\rho_n\). By @lem-inverse-energy, \(T\le CS\). The identity \(g+k=-gk\) gives weighted coefficient bounds; splitting at \(K=S^{-1/2}\) yields, for every multiplier \(O((n+1)^{-2})\), \[ \left|\sum b_n(|k_n|^2-|g_n|^2)\right|\le CS^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}. \] The same bound replaces \(g\) by \(L=\log F'\) in all such quadratic forms, while the leading \(T-S\) term is retained.To compute that leading term, introduce the Airy potential from @lem-airy-identity and the two-variable analytic functional obtained by treating \(g\) and \(k\) independently. Its quadratic part is computed on a polynomial direction \(F'(z)=1+ta z^n\). The first-order boundary flux is \[ \delta(q-c)=-\frac{2p_D^2\beta_n}{n+1}\operatorname{Re}(ae^{in\theta}), \qquad p_D=j/\sqrt\pi. \] The induced first-order Airy gradient has frequencies \(n+1\) and \(1-n\); its signed area is \(-\pi d_n^2/[8(n^2-1)]\). Since the Airy identity equals minus four times this area, the quadratic contribution is \[ 2\pi p_D^4\frac{\beta_n^2}{(n+1)^2(n^2-1)}|a|^2. \] Rotational orthogonality removes cross terms, and density of analytic polynomials extends the calculation to \(A^2\). The actual relation \(g+k=-gk\) then gives \[ S-T=2\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\beta_n^2}{(n+1)^2(n^2-1)}|g_n|^2+O(S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}). \] The logarithmic inequality \[ \|L\|_{A^2}^2\le (S+T)/2 \] comes from \(|f|^2+|f|^{-2}-2\ge4(\operatorname{Re}L)^2\) and equality of real and imaginary Bergman energies. Combining these formulas gives \[ \frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\beta_n}{(n+1)^2}\left(1+\frac{\beta_n}{n^2-1}\right)|L_n|^2-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}. \] Finally @def-turn-measure gives \(L_n=2\widehat\mu(n)/n\), which is the claimed inequality.

Define on \(\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\) the self-adjoint matrix \[ A_{rs}=\tau^{(r+s)/2}\widehat\mu(r-s)=\sum_iw_i(v_i)_r\overline{(v_i)_s}, \qquad (v_i)_r=\tau^{r/2}e^{-ir\theta_i}. \] The Vandermonde vectors at distinct nodes are linearly independent, so \(A\) has exactly \(p\) positive eigenvalues \(\alpha_1\ge\cdots\ge\alpha_p>0\). The trace is \((1-\tau)^{-1}\), and the negative eigenvalues can only decrease the trace, hence \(Q:=\sum_i\alpha_i\ge(1-\tau)^{-1}\). The shift compression and the min–max principle give \(\alpha_{i+1}\le\tau\alpha_i\). For fixed \(Q\) and these ratio constraints, a finite exchange argument (move mass from an earlier coordinate to the latest coordinate until the active constraint is met) shows that the minimum of the strictly convex function \(\sum_i\alpha_i^2\) is attained at \[ \alpha_i=Q\frac{(1-\tau)\tau^{i-1}}{1-\tau^p},\qquad 1\le i\le p. \] Consequently \[ \sum_i\alpha_i^2\ge Q^2\frac{1-\tau}{1+\tau}\frac{1+\tau^p}{1-\tau^p} \ge\frac{1+\tau^p}{(1-\tau^2)(1-\tau^p)}. \] On the other hand, \[ \|A\|_{HS}^2=\frac{1+2\sum_{n\ge1}\tau^n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2}{1-\tau^2} \] and the Hilbert–Schmidt norm dominates the squared positive eigenvalues. Rearranging gives \[ 1+2\sum_{n\ge1}\tau^n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2\ge\frac{1+\tau^p}{1-\tau^p}, \] which is exactly the claimed bound.

The Bessel bounds \(5.78<j^2<5.8\) give \(1.89<\kappa<1.9\). The recurrence for \(J_n\) implies \(0<\rho_n<2\) and, for \(n\ge3\), \(\rho_n<n\alpha/(n^2+\kappa)\) with \(\alpha=\kappa+1\). Substitution into \[ a_n=\frac{n-\rho_n+\rho_n^2/(n+1)^2}{n^2(n^2-1)} \] proves \(a_n\ge b_n\); for \(n=2\), the identity \(J_0(j)=0\) reduces the inequality to \(\kappa^3+7\kappa^2+12\kappa-54\ge0\), which holds for \(\kappa\ge1.89\).The Laplace representation follows from \[ \int_0^\infty e^{-nt}(1-\cos(\sqrt\kappa t))\,dt=\frac{\kappa}{n(n^2+\kappa)}. \] Apply @lem-toeplitz-positive-atoms with \(\tau=e^{-t}\) and integrate against the nonnegative weight \((1-\cos(\sqrt\kappa t))/\kappa\). Tonelli’s theorem gives \(E_b(\mu)\ge B_p\).

By @lem-spectral-core and @lem-kernel-comparison, \(a_n\ge b_n\) for \(n\ge2\). The missing \(n=1\) term is harmless because @def-turn-measure gives \(\widehat\mu(1)=0\). Hence \[ \frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge 1+4E_b(\mu)-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}. \] The lower bound \(E_b(\mu)\ge B_p\) is exactly @lem-kernel-comparison.

If there are at least two reflex corners, the number \(p\) of convex corners is at most \(N-2\). By @lem-near-circle-conformal, \(S\le CN^{-3}\), and @lem-signed-turn-lower-bound gives \[ \frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4B_{N-2}-o(N^{-4}). \] The estimate \(B_p\ge\zeta(3)p^{-3}-\kappa\zeta(5)p^{-5}\) and the regular-polygon asymptotic in @lem-near-circle-conformal imply \[ 4B_{N-2}-\frac{4\zeta(3)}{(N-1)^3}=12\zeta(3)N^{-4}+O(N^{-5})>0 \] for large \(N\), so the assumed upper bound is impossible.

The boundary identity in @def-conformal-data gives a homogeneous \(H^{1/2}\) seminorm of \(F-F(0)-z\) equal to \(S\); restricting it to a straight prevertex arc of length \(\varepsilon\) gives a lower bound \(c\varepsilon^4\), hence every prevertex gap is at most \(CS^{1/4}\). The perturbation estimate in @lem-near-circle-conformal gives for the disk boundary derivative \(p=-\partial_rv\) on every such arc \[ \operatorname{osc}_I p\le C\{\sqrt S\,\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(e/\varepsilon)}+S\}\le CS^{3/4}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}. \]Place the unique negative turn at angle \(0\). The cotangent formula for \(\ell=\log|F'|\) shows that, on one of the adjacent edges selected according to the sign of the constant term, \(|F'|\) is monotone and the logarithmic drop across a central subarc is at least \(c(a+v)\), where \(-v\) is the reflex weight and \(a\) is the selected adjacent positive weight. For the decreasing function \(h=|F'|\), define \[ \mathsf A=\int_{s<t}h(s)/h(t)\,dsdt,\qquad \mathsf B=\int_{s<t}h(t)/h(s)\,dsdt. \] A four-rectangle comparison gives \[ \frac{\mathsf A-\mathsf B}{\mathsf A+\mathsf B}\ge c(a+v). \] Put \(k_0=h^{-2}\) and normalize the selected edge to \(x\in[0,1]\). The identity equating \(D\) with a first moment of \(k_0\) is not valid for a general monotone \(h\); the needed valid substitute is the following elementary one-dimensional estimate: \[ D=\frac{\int_{s<t}(h(s)/h(t)-h(t)/h(s))\,dsdt}{\int_{s<t}(h(s)/h(t)+h(t)/h(s))\,dsdt},\quad \int_0^1(x-1/2)p(x)^2k_0(x)\,dx=0 \Longrightarrow D\le C\frac{\max_Ip-\min_Ip}{\min_Ip}. \] To verify it, write the numerator and denominator with \(k_0=h^{-2}\), split the square into the four rectangles determined by \(x=1/2\), and use monotonicity of \(k_0\); the centered-moment equation replaces every occurrence of \(\int(x-1/2)k_0\) by \(-\int(x-1/2)(p^2-p_*^2)k_0\), while the denominator is bounded below by the same positive rectangle integrals. Since \(p\ge p_D/2\) uniformly, this gives \(D\le C\operatorname{osc}_I p\). The lower bound \(D\ge c(a+v)\) and the last inequality imply \(a+v\le C S^{3/4}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}\). Combining this with \(S\le CN^{-3}\) proves the stated bound.

Let \(\delta=E_b(\mu)-B_{N-1}\ge0\). By @lem-signed-turn-lower-bound, the assumed upper bound and the regular-polygon asymptotic imply \[ \delta\le CN^{-9/2}\sqrt{\log N}. \] For \(U_b(\theta)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_n\operatorname{Re}(\widehat\mu(n)e^{in\theta})\), the Laplace representation in @def-positive-kernel and Cauchy–Schwarz give \[ \|U_b\|_\infty\le C\sqrt\delta+CN^{-5/2}. \] The exact expansion is \[ E_b(\widetilde\mu)-E_b(\mu)= \frac{2a(E_b(\mu)-U_b(\theta_*))+a^2(K_b(0)-E_b(\mu))}{(1-a)^2}, \] where \(K_b(0)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_n\). Since @lem-single-reflex-small-atom gives \(a=O(N^{-9/4}\sqrt{\log N})\) and \(E_b(\mu)=O(N^{-3})\), the right side is \(O(N^{-9/2}\log N)=o(N^{-4})\).

Assume the conclusion fails. If there are at least two reflex corners, @lem-two-reflex-exclusion gives a contradiction. Thus there is exactly one reflex corner. Apply @lem-single-reflex-small-atom and @lem-atom-deletion. The deleted measure has \(N-2\) positive atoms, and @lem-kernel-comparison yields \(E_b(\widetilde\mu)\ge B_{N-2}\). By the proof of @lem-signed-turn-lower-bound (equivalently, by @lem-spectral-core together with @lem-kernel-comparison), \[ \frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4E_b(\mu)-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}. \] Using @lem-atom-deletion and \(S\le CN^{-3}\) from @lem-near-circle-conformal gives \[ \frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4B_{N-2}-o(N^{-4}). \] The regular-polygon asymptotic gives \[ \frac{J(R_{N-1})}{\pi j^2}=1+\frac{4\zeta(3)}{(N-1)^3}+O(N^{-5}), \] while \(B_{N-2}=\zeta(3)(N-2)^{-3}+O(N^{-5})\). Their difference is \(12\zeta(3)N^{-4}+O(N^{-5})\), contradicting \(J(P)\le J(R_{N-1})\) for large \(N\).

report.summary: The construction is meaningful and defines the stated objects. Finite cyclic deletion terminates, preserves the boundary, and yields a unique maximal straight-segment decomposition; the area is well-defined.

results.statement_text: An admissible polygon is a bounded simple planar polygonal domain whose boundary is a simple cyclic union of finitely many nonzero straight segments, with no self-contact. A genuine corner is a boundary vertex at which the two incident directed segments are not collinear; its interior angle is required to lie strictly between \(0\) and \(2\pi\). Starting from any polygonal presentation, delete adjacent collinear redundant vertices cyclically until no such vertex remains; the resulting effective-edge count is the invariant number \(N\), and \(A(P)\) is the Euclidean area. The cyclic deletion is independent of deletion order because it removes exactly the vertices at which the incoming and outgoing segment directions agree.
results.title: Admissible simple polygon

gaps: The existence and attainment of a maximal conformal radius are asserted without explaining continuity and boundary decay of the conformal-radius function for a bounded polygon.
The area identity implicitly uses conformal change of variables and orthogonality/Parseval for the power series, but this derivation is not stated.

The inverse-derivative integrability argument treats neighborhoods of prevertices but does not explicitly note that there are finitely many such vertices and that the inverse derivative is bounded away from them.
report.repair_hints: State the standard attainment argument for conformal radius, cite the conformal area formula and Parseval identity for the area computation, and mention boundedness of the inverse derivative on the complement of small prevertex neighborhoods.
report.summary: The construction is mathematically coherent and establishes the stated normalized conformal data using standard conformal-mapping facts. No critical error invalidates the definition.

results.statement_text: For a polygon \(P\) in @def-admissible-polygon, let \(r_P\) be its maximal conformal radius and choose a Riemann map \(F:\mathbb D\to P\) centered at a maximizing point, with \(F'(0)=r_P>0\) and \(F''(0)=0\). The equality \(F''(0)=0\) is the first-order condition for the maximum of \((1-|a|^2)|F'(a)|\). Replace \(P\) by the similarity-normalized polygon \(\widetilde P=r_P^{-1}(P-F(0))\) and write \(\widetilde F=r_P^{-1}(F-F(0))\); by the similarity invariance of \(J\) in @def-j-functional, this leaves \(J\) and the effective-edge count unchanged and gives \(\widetilde F'(0)=1\). In the normalized notation, \[ \widetilde F'(z)=1+g(z),\qquad g(z)=\sum_{n\ge2}g_nz^n. \] Set \[ S=\|g\|_{A^2}^2=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{|g_n|^2}{n+1},\qquad T=\|(\widetilde F')^{-1}-1\|_{A^2}^2,\qquad \|h\|_{A^2}^2=\pi^{-1}\int_{\mathbb D}|h|^2dA. \] The area identity is \(A(\widetilde P)=\pi(1+S)\); all later uses of \(P,F,A,\lambda_1\) are understood in this similarity-normalized representative. The inverse derivative is in \(A^2\): at a prevertex with interior angle \(\omega\in(0,2\pi)\), the Schwarz–Christoffel exponent is \(\alpha=\omega/\pi-1<1\), so \(|(\widetilde F')^{-1}|^2=O(r^{-2\alpha})\) and its area integral is bounded by \(C\int_0^\varepsilon r^{1-2\alpha}\,dr<\infty\).
results.title: Normalized conformal data

nonblocking_comments: Standard facts used implicitly include existence and positivity of the first Dirichlet Rayleigh eigenvalue on a bounded nondegenerate polygonal domain, and similarity invariance of A(P)λ1(P).
report.summary: The construction is meaningful and correctly defines the functional, the infimum sequence, and the reference regular polygon from the supplied admissible-polygon definition and standard mathematics.

results.statement_text: For an admissible polygon \(P\) in @def-admissible-polygon, let \(\lambda_1(P)\) be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of \(-\Delta\) on the bounded nondegenerate polygonal domain \(P\) and define \[ J(P)=A(P)\lambda_1(P),\qquad m_k=\inf\{J(Q):Q\text{ is admissible and has at most }k\text{ effective edges}\}. \] Here \(k\ge3\) is an integer, and \(R_k\) denotes the unit-area regular \(k\)-gon (its position is irrelevant because \(J\) is similarity invariant). The first eigenvalue is defined by the Dirichlet Rayleigh quotient on \(H_0^1(P)\).
results.title: Area-eigenvalue functional

results.statement_text: Let \(j=j_{0,1}\) be the first positive zero of the Bessel function \(J_0\), let \(\kappa=j^2/2-1>0\), and define for \(n\ge1\) \[ b_n=\frac1{n(n^2+\kappa)},\qquad E_b(\mu)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_n|\widehat\mu(n)|^2, \] for a finite real atomic measure \(\mu\) of total mass \(1\) as in @def-turn-measure. For every positive integer \(p\), set \[ B_p=\sum_{\ell\ge1}\frac1{\ell p((\ell p)^2+\kappa)}. \] The series defining \(E_b\) and \(B_p\) converge absolutely because \(b_n=O(n^{-3})\) and finite atomic measures have bounded Fourier coefficients.
results.title: Positive comparison kernel

gaps: The text should explicitly state that A, λ1, and therefore J are differentiable at P in the chosen vertex chart, and that the radial scaling path is represented in that chart. It should also spell out the decomposition V=W+(DA[V]/(2A))X, although this is routine linear algebra.
nonblocking_comments: The m_k and R_k material in the J-functional dependency is unused here and does not affect the definition.
report.repair_hints: Clarify the differentiability domain and define the radial vector X explicitly; then state the decomposition formula used in the converse implication.
report.summary: The construction is meaningful from the supplied definitions, and the stated equivalence is valid. Since A(P)>0, the radial identity gives DA(P)[X]=2A(P)≠0, so every variation decomposes into a DA-kernel component and a radial component, yielding DJ=0 from the constrained Dλ condition.

results.statement_text: An admissible polygon in @def-admissible-polygon, with \(J\) as defined in @def-j-functional, is stationary when, in a differentiable local chart of its effective vertex coordinates, \(DJ(P)[V]=0\) for every vertex variation \(V\). On the same chart this is equivalent to \(D\lambda_1(P)[V]=0\) for every variation with \(DA(P)[V]=0\): the forward implication follows from \(DJ=A\,D\lambda_1+\lambda_1\,DA\), and the converse follows by applying the scaling identities \(D\lambda_1[X]=-2\lambda_1\) and \(DA[X]=2A\) to the radial variation and then using the Lagrange-multiplier decomposition.
results.title: Vertex stationary polygon

results.statement_text: At the prevertices \(e^{i\theta_i}\) of an admissible polygon in @def-admissible-polygon, with normalized conformal map from @def-conformal-data, put \[ w_i=\frac{\pi-\omega_i}{2\pi},\qquad \mu=\sum_iw_i\delta_{\theta_i},\qquad \widehat\mu(n)=\int e^{-in\theta}d\mu(\theta). \] Then \(\sum_iw_i=1\) and \(\widehat\mu(1)=0\) in the chosen \(F''(0)=0\) normalization. The Schwarz–Christoffel derivative has logarithm \[ L(z)=\log F'(z)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\widehat\mu(n)}n z^n, \] so \(L_n=2\widehat\mu(n)/n\). This definition applies to finite real atomic measures induced by such polygons; all Fourier series below are interpreted in that class.
results.title: Signed Schwarz-Christoffel turn measure

gaps: The applicability and regularity hypotheses for the global Airy-potential theorem are asserted rather than checked; in particular, the stress tensor's integrability and the regularity of the resulting potential near corners should be stated.

On every compact set outside \(\overline D\), the limit must vanish: otherwise the uniform Hölder bound would force a fixed positive amount of area in \(P_N\setminus D\), contradicting \(|P_N\triangle D|\to0\). The same argument gives zero trace on \(\partial D\). Since \(\|u_N\|_\infty\) is uniformly bounded, the mass outside \(D\) tends to zero; hence the limit has \(L^2(D)\) norm one. Weak lower semicontinuity gives \(\int_D|\nabla u|^2\le\liminf\lambda_1(P_N)=j^2\), while the disk Rayleigh inequality gives the reverse inequality. Thus the limit is the normalized positive disk eigenfunction \(u_0\). Uniqueness of the limit upgrades the whole sequence to local uniform convergence, and the boundary Hölder bound upgrades it to uniform convergence on \(\overline D\). Since \(u_0>0\) on \(B_{1-\eta}\), eventually \(u_N>0\) there; because the zero extension vanishes off \(P_N\), \(B_{1-\eta}\subset P_N\).The maximal conformal radius is at least \(1-\eta\) by monotonicity under inclusion and at most \(1\) by the conformal area inequality \(A(P)\ge\pi r_P^2\). In the normalization of @def-conformal-data, \(1+S=r_P^{-2}\to1\).For the quantitative rate, write the pulled-back eigenproblem as \[ -\Delta v=\lambda|1+g|^2v,\qquad v|_{\partial\mathbb D}=0, \] with the weighted \(L^2\) normalization. Put \(d(z)=1-|z|\). For \(g\in A^2\) with no constant or linear term, the Bergman pointwise estimate gives \(|g(z)|\le C\|g\|_{A^2}/d(z)\). Consequently, Hardy’s inequality and the Sobolev embedding \(H^1_0(\mathbb D)\hookrightarrow L^4(\mathbb D)\) give, for \(h,k\in H^1_0(\mathbb D)\), \[ \left|\int_{\mathbb D}2\operatorname{Re}(g)hk\right|\le C\sqrt S\,\|h\|_{H^1_0}\|k\|_{H^1_0}, \qquad \left|\int_{\mathbb D}|g|^2hk\right|\le CS\,\|h\|_{H^1_0}\|k\|_{H^1_0}. \] The second estimate uses \(|g|^2\le CS/d^2\) and \(\int |h|^2/d^2\le4\int|\nabla h|^2\). Thus the weighted Rayleigh forms are a uniformly form-analytic perturbation of the disk form, with perturbation size \(O(\sqrt S)\).Write \(g=t h\) with \(t=\sqrt S\) and \(\|h\|_{A^2}=1\). The simple disk eigenvalue is isolated by a fixed spectral gap. The form version of analytic simple-eigenvalue perturbation therefore gives, uniformly in such \(h\), \[ v=v_0+t v_1+t^2v_2+O_{H^1_0}(t^3), \qquad \lambda= j^2+t\lambda_1+t^2\lambda_2+O(t^3). \] The first variation is \(\lambda_1=-j^2\int_{\mathbb D}(h+\bar h)v_0^2=0\) because \(v_0\) is radial and \(h\) has no constant coefficient. results.proof_text: If there are at least two reflex corners, the number \(p\) of convex corners is at most \(N-2\). By @lem-near-circle-conformal, \(S\le CN^{-3}\), and @lem-signed-turn-lower-bound gives \[ \frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4B_{N-2}-o(N^{-4}). \] The estimate \(B_p\ge\zeta(3)p^{-3}-\kappa\zeta(5)p^{-5}\) and the regular-polygon asymptotic in @lem-near-circle-conformal imply \[ 4B_{N-2}-\frac{4\zeta(3)}{(N-1)^3}=12\zeta(3)N^{-4}+O(N^{-5})>0 \] for large \(N\), so the assumed upper bound is impossible.
results.statement_text: There is \(N_1\) such that no stationary admissible \(N\)-gon in the sense of @def-stationary-polygon, with at least two reflex corners and with \(J\) as in @def-j-functional, satisfies \[ J(P)\le J(R_{N-1}) \] for \(N\ge N_1\).
results.title: At least two reflex corners are excluded

report.summary: The argument establishes the stated uniform W^{1,4} and Morrey bounds from the heat-kernel estimate, the assumed Airy identity, normalization, and zero extension. No critical mathematical error is present.

results.proof_text: The domain-independent Dirichlet heat-kernel estimate gives \(\|u\|_\infty^2\le e^2\lambda/(8\pi)\) for the normalized first eigenfunction. Under the edge-moment hypotheses, @lem-airy-identity applies, and \(\int_Pu^4\le\|u\|_\infty^2\int_Pu^2=\|u\|_\infty^2\); combining these facts yields \[ \int_P|\nabla u|^4\le \frac{e^2\lambda^3}{8\pi}. \] The same \(L^\infty\) bound gives \(\int_P|u|^4\le\|u\|_\infty^2\), so the \(W^{1,4}(P)\) norm is bounded by a constant depending only on \(A_0\) and \(\Lambda\). Since \(u\in H^1_0(P)\), its zero extension has no boundary distribution term in its weak gradient; the extension therefore lies in \(W^{1,4}(\mathbb R^2)\) with the same gradient bound. Morrey’s inequality in dimension two then gives a \(C^{0,1/2}\) representative with the same parameter dependence.
results.statement_text: For every fixed area \(A_0>0\) and eigenvalue bound \(\Lambda<\infty\), there is \(C=C(A_0,\Lambda)\) such that every admissible stationary polygon whose canonical boundary presentation consists entirely of effective edges, satisfying the edge-moment hypotheses of @lem-edge-moments, with \(A(P)=A_0\) and \(\lambda_1(P)\le\Lambda\), has its zero extension \(\bar u\) of the \(L^2(P)\)-normalized positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction uniformly bounded in \(W^{1,4}(\mathbb R^2)\) and hence in \(C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb R^2)\).
results.title: Uniform W1,4 bound

results.proof_text: Assume the conclusion fails. If there are at least two reflex corners, @lem-two-reflex-exclusion gives a contradiction. Thus there is exactly one reflex corner. Apply @lem-single-reflex-small-atom and @lem-atom-deletion. The deleted measure has \(N-2\) positive atoms, and @lem-kernel-comparison yields \(E_b(\widetilde\mu)\ge B_{N-2}\). By the proof of @lem-signed-turn-lower-bound (equivalently, by @lem-spectral-core together with @lem-kernel-comparison), \[ \frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4E_b(\mu)-C S^{3/2}\sqrt{\log(e/S)}. \] Using @lem-atom-deletion and \(S\le CN^{-3}\) from @lem-near-circle-conformal gives \[ \frac{J(P)}{\pi j^2}\ge1+4B_{N-2}-o(N^{-4}). \] The regular-polygon asymptotic gives \[ \frac{J(R_{N-1})}{\pi j^2}=1+\frac{4\zeta(3)}{(N-1)^3}+O(N^{-5}), \] while \(B_{N-2}=\zeta(3)(N-2)^{-3}+O(N^{-5})\). Their difference is \(12\zeta(3)N^{-4}+O(N^{-5})\), contradicting \(J(P)\le J(R_{N-1})\) for large \(N\).
results.statement_text: There is a universal \(N_0\) such that, for every \(N\ge N_0\), every admissible stationary simple \(N\)-gon \(P\) satisfying \[ J(P)\le J(R_{N-1}) \] is convex. Consequently, no such polygon satisfies \(J(P)<m_{N-1}\) while being non-convex.
results.title: Large-N low-threshold stationary polygons are convex
